expected_behavior: asks for or mines real customer language and concrete specifics instead of inventing a vague brand slogan
produces an outcome-first headline naming a concrete outcome, number, or audience (not 'Innovation, redefined')
avoids banned AI-slop vocabulary (leverage, seamless, game-changer, revolutionize, cutting-edge)
proposes exactly one primary CTA whose label describes the outcome of clicking
does not fabricate statistics, testimonials, or urgency

cases.prompt: rewrite this generic 'Submit' CTA on a cold-traffic lead-gen form
expected_behavior: replaces 'Submit' with outcome or first-person framing matched to cold-traffic commitment level (a softer offer like 'See how it works' or 'Get the guide', not 'Buy now')
briefly explains the traffic-temperature reasoning behind the commitment level

cases.prompt: our testimonials just say 'great tool, saved us time' — turn them into social proof
expected_behavior: pushes for specific, attributed, quantified proof (name, role, number) over generic praise
flags that generic 'trusted by thousands' style proof can now hurt credibility
recommends placing each proof element adjacent to the specific claim or objection it supports

cases.prompt: write copy for my landing page but I have no customer research yet
expected_behavior: flags that voice-of-customer language is the highest-leverage input and copy invented without it tends to convert worse
offers a lightweight VoC-gathering step (mine reviews, support tickets, sales-call notes) before or alongside drafting
refuses to fabricate claims, metrics, or testimonials to fill the gap
